candidates.title: PRT player claim path hashes and keeps every output of the current input: memory grows with the output count and each tx-output yield costs a read and keccak of up to 2 MiB, whatever the guest spent
candidates.role: Support (AUDIT.md: 'The PRT player and bridge in doc/recipes ... Support'). It stands in for the honest operator: it computes the epoch claim.
candidates.location: doc/recipes/prt.lua: player_meta.__index:run_next_input (about lines 2241-2272, always passes last_output = {} and self.outputs_frontier); player_meta.__index:run_to_input_mcycle_offset (about lines 2066-2124: pending_output_hashes, on_yield_automatic at 2080-2091, flush_pending_outputs at 2105-2117); run_to_stop (1396-1409); receive_cmio_request (972-976) -> src/machine.cpp machine::receive_cmio_request (1986-2017, available_length = min(tohost_data, AR_CMIO_TX_BUFFER_LENGTH)).
candidates.description: run_next_input advances the epoch machine and builds the epoch computation hash (the honest claim) through run_to_input_mcycle_offset. It always passes last_output = {} (truthy), so on_yield_automatic is installed for every input. For every automatic yield with reason tx-output, the callback calls machine:receive_cmio_request(), which copies min(declared length, 2 MiB) bytes out of the tx buffer into a Lua string, hashes it with keccak, and appends the hash to pending_output_hashes. That table is only flushed (into the O(log) outputs frontier) when the input ends with an accepted manual yield; until then it holds one entry per output, so the player's memory grows linearly with the number of outputs of the current input. The table is needed only to discard the outputs of a rejected input; a copy of the 64-entry frontier taken at the input boundary would give the same result in bounded memory. Separately, the bytes read and hashed per output are the length the guest declares in tohost, not bytes the guest wrote in that output: a guest that fills the tx buffer once and then yields tx-output with length 2^21 in a two-instruction loop makes the player read and hash 2 MiB per 2 mcycles.
candidates.trigger: Guest code that an input has taken over (or any application) loops on an automatic yield with reason tx-output: 'sd t1, 0(HTIF tohost); j' with t1 = yield|automatic|tx-output|len. With len = 8 and a changing payload, each output costs the guest 4 mcycles and the player ~121 bytes of retained Lua memory; with len = 2 MiB (contents written once), each output costs the guest 2 mcycles and the player ~5.3 ms of CPU. The input never needs to finish: the memory is held until the input ends (accept), and if it ends in a rejection, at imcyclemax or never, the table is kept for the whole input.
candidates.reachability: Reachable from any valid template: the guest writes tohost through the HTIF device with only instruction semantics, and automatic yields are enabled in every template that follows the rollup interface (the manual's default configuration sets the yield bits). No input sequence restriction applies; one input that takes over the guest suffices. The per-input mcycle budget is up to 2^48 mcycles (ROLLUP_LOG2_MAX_MCYCLES_PER_ADVANCE_STATE), so the table can reach ~2^46 entries, far above any host memory.
rating_steps: 1. Out of scope? The trigger is guest code, which the model treats as fully adversarial (section 4). The exclusion 'An application that tries to exhaust the honest operator through the number of its outputs or yields ... holds as long as the memory and storage that the honest operator needs to defend its claims do not grow with the number of outputs, and each yield costs it a bounded amount (R12)' does not apply, because its condition fails here: the memory the claim path needs grows with outputs. 'Keeping outputs to prove them later is not on the honest operator's path' -- the player keeps them on its claim path, unconditionally. Also 'The entries about applications exclude what an application loses, never an emulator defect that its guest triggers'. Not out of scope.

2. Role: the defect is only in the PRT player, a Support component standing in for the honest operator ('implementations of an operator that no deployment runs'). Section 3: 'A defect that only a support component shows is Medium when it would rate High or Critical in the role the component stands in for, such as ... the honest operator for an implementation of an operator or a tool that computes claims.' The emulator's own receive_cmio_request is bounded (2 MiB) and is not the defect.

3. High/Medium cases, in the honest-operator role: R12 'The memory and storage the honest operator needs to defend its claims do not grow with the number of outputs.' and 'Each of the following operations has a worst case in host time and memory that is bounded and at most linear in the cycles it executes' -- here memory is linear in outputs (violating the explicit no-growth clause) and the host time per 2-mcycle yield is a 2 MiB read+keccak (a constant factor ~10^6 over an mcycle). Section 8 Critical: 'An operation listed in R12 whose worst-case cost a guest can make unbounded, super-linear, or larger than what the deployment was sized for.' The memory growth is unbounded within an input (2^48 mcycles). In the honest-operator role this would be Critical (R12 violated at a reachable state on the honest operator's path); otherwise at least High ('multiply the worst-case cost ... by a constant factor').

4. Critical in the stood-in role (R12, R4 'No reachable state makes ... exceed its resource bounds (R12)'): the player can run out of memory while computing the honest claim, so the honest claim cannot be computed ('Completeness failure. The honest operator ... cannot respond in time').
5. Final: support component -> capped at Medium (section 3/8 step 2).
candidates.threat_to_goal: If a production operator behaved like the player (and the player is the shipped reference of how to compute claims), one input could make the honest operator exhaust memory, or spend ~5 ms per 2 guest mcycles, while computing its epoch claim; the honest claim then cannot be posted or defended in time and a dishonest claim wins by timeout (completeness failure). Because the model says the operator's memory must not grow with outputs, this is a rule violation independent of the deployment's sizing.
candidates.evidence: Ran /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/blind10/PERGUEST/playerlike.lua (a copy of run_to_stop + on_yield_automatic: machine:run, receive_cmio_request, keccak256, append to table) with bare-metal guests built by bugs/harness/baremetal/build.sh: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/blind10/PERGUEST/g/ayieldvar.S (tx-output len 8, counter payload): 800000 mcycles -> 199998 outputs, 23.6 MiB retained, 121 B/output (linear). /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/blind10/PERGUEST/g/ayieldbig.S (tx-output len 2^21, tx buffer never written): 400 mcycles -> 197 outputs, 1.04 s CPU, 5.3 ms/output (vs ~3 ns per mcycle for a plain loop).
candidates.test_idea: Build the ayieldvar guest into a rolling template whose first input's code loops on tx-output yields K times and then yields manual accepted with a garbage root (or simply never accepts). Load prt.lua's player module with a stub chain and call run_next_input on that input while sampling collectgarbage('count'); assert the player's retained memory after K outputs is bounded by a constant independent of K (e.g. run K=10^5 and K=10^6 and require the difference < 1 MiB). Fails today (~110 MB difference). A second assertion: with the ayieldbig guest, the player's CPU per guest mcycle must stay within a fixed constant of the plain-loop cost (e.g. < 100x); fails today (~10^6x).

candidates.title: collect_mcycle_root_hashes returns at every automatic yield and rehashes the shadow state on each return and re-entry, so a yield loop makes every mcycle of a claim cost as much as a sampled one (~6000x at large periods)
candidates.location: src/machine.cpp machine::collect_mcycle_root_hashes: update_hash_tree() at entry (line 2451, which also marks the 'always dirty' shadow registers, shadow TLB and shadow uarch pages, machine.cpp 1645-1648 and machine-address-ranges.cpp 129-134); unconditional m_ht.update(m_ars) after every interpret return, sampling point or not (line 2520); early return on any break other than reached_target_mcycle, including yielded_automatically (line 2558). src/collect-mcycle-hashes-state-access.hpp do_write_mcycle (lines 150-158) marks all 8 pages of AR_SHADOW_STATE_LENGTH (registers + the 6 TLB pages) dirty on every interpreter exit. doc/recipes/prt.lua mcycle_computation_hash_run / run_to_stop show the honest caller re-entering after each yield.
candidates.description: An automatic yield is not a sampling point and the computation hash does not need any hash there, yet each one costs two hash-tree updates over at least the 8 shadow pages: one inside the loop right after interpret returns (m_ht.update runs before the phase test) and one at the next call's entry (update_hash_tree, which re-marks the shadow registers, the whole shadow TLB and the shadow uarch state dirty). do_write_mcycle also marks the 6 shadow TLB pages dirty on every exit even when no TLB slot changed (do_write_tlb already marks its own page). The per-yield host cost is therefore about the cost of a period-1 sample (~18-20 us here), while run() handles the same yield in ~0.3 us. A guest that yields automatically every 2 mcycles makes the mcycle-level claim cost ~20 us per mcycle at any sampling period, versus ~3 ns per mcycle for ordinary code at a large period.
candidates.trigger: Guest code looping on 'sd t1, 0(tohost); j' with an automatic yield (any automatic reason, e.g. progress or tx-output with length 0). The honest operator (and the player as its stand-in) must keep calling collect_mcycle_root_hashes after every yield to finish the claim.
candidates.reachability: Reachable from any valid template: automatic yields are enabled by default and are issued through the HTIF device by plain stores; any instruction stream a taken-over guest runs is reachable.
rating_steps: 1. Out of scope? Possibly, by 'An application that tries to exhaust the honest operator through the number of its outputs or yields. Each costs the guest mcycles ... as long as ... each yield costs it a bounded amount (R12).' The per-yield cost is bounded (a constant ~20-40 us). Against that, the trigger is an input-controlled guest, not the application's design, and 'The entries about applications exclude what an application loses, never an emulator defect that its guest triggers (R4, R5, R8)'. The deciding fact is whether triage reads 'bounded amount per yield' as excusing any constant, or whether section 8's High clause on constant factors still applies to yields. Give both.
2. Role: collect_mcycle_root_hashes is listed as Honest operator in the AUDIT.md component table.

3. High/Medium cases: High 'A defect that lets the guest ... multiply the worst-case cost of an operation listed in R12 by a constant factor, compared with the same operation without the defect, while staying within what the deployment was sized for. A cost that the specified semantics require is not a defect. When the sizing is unknown, rate such a constant-factor increase High'. The operation is 'a part of a claim' (R12). The semantics require a hash only at sampling points and fixed points; nothing requires hashing at an automatic yield, and run() shows the yield itself costs ~0.3 us. Measured factor: ~6000x per mcycle at log2 period 30 (3.2 ns -> 19.5 us per mcycle), ~700x at log2 period 10 (28 ns -> 20 us).

4. Critical only if the deployment was sized from ordinary per-mcycle cost and the factor pushes the epoch claim beyond the clocks ('larger than what the deployment was sized for'); sizing unknown, so not claimed.
5. If step 1 excludes it: Low/Out of scope (average performance).
candidates.claimed_severity: High (or Out of scope under the yields exclusion; triage to decide)
candidates.threat_to_goal: The honest operator must finish the epoch claim within the clocks (A7). A guest that spends its input budget on automatic yields raises the operator's cost of the top-level computation hash by three to four orders of magnitude over ordinary code at the same mcycle count, which a deployment sized on typical per-mcycle cost would not cover; the honest claim could then be posted too late (completeness failure).
candidates.evidence: Ran /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/blind10/PERGUEST/cost.lua (loop: collect_mcycle_root_hashes(target, log2p, phase, 0) until target; then the same span with run()) with guests /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/blind10/PERGUEST/g/spin.S (addi loop) and /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/blind10/PERGUEST/g/ayield.S (automatic tx-output len 0 loop). log2p=10: spin 27.9 ns/mcycle (1 call), ayield 20144 ns/mcycle (99999 calls), run() on ayield 147.6 ns/mcycle. log2p=30: spin 3.2 ns/mcycle, ayield 19485 ns/mcycle. log2p=0 (every mcycle sampled): spin 18235 ns/mcycle, i.e. a yield costs about the same as a sample. /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/blind10/PERGUEST/rh.lua: get_root_hash 4 us/call, collect call that executes nothing 10 us/call.
candidates.test_idea: With the ayield guest (automatic yield every 2 mcycles) and the spin guest, compute the full mcycle computation hash over the same span (e.g. 2^20 mcycles, log2 period 20) through collect_mcycle_root_hashes, re-entering after each yield as prt.lua does; also run the same span with run(). Assert that time(ayield, collect) <= C * time(ayield, run()) + time(spin, collect) for a small constant C (e.g. 10), or, deterministically, count hash-tree page rehashes (cartesi hash-tree stats if exposed, or a counter around m_ht.update) and assert that collection over a span with Y automatic yields and S sampling points rehashes O(S + dirty pages) pages, not O(Y * 8). Fails today (each yield rehashes >= 8 pages twice).

not_covered: Worst-case uarch cycles of a single main-processor step (Sv57 page walk with fetch crossing a page, soft-float FMA/FDIV/FSQRT on subnormals, interrupt + exception in the same mcycle): reasoned the 2^20 budget is ample but did not measure the maximum.

Exhaustive check that every instruction that can make an interrupt pending and enabled returns success_and_serve_interrupts (the uarch keeps asserts on, so a miss would be a uarch trap): checked CSR writes (mstatus/sstatus/mie/sie/mip/sip/mideleg), MRET/SRET, CLINT msip/mtimecmp and PLIC claim/complete; did not audit raise_exception and every CSR set/clear path (CSRRS/CSRRC with rs1=x0) line by line.

Stale cached translation (shadow/hot TLB) equivalence between native, collect, record/replay and the uarch bridge under adversarial PMA index/vp_offset sequences; only read the uarch bridge and the write_tlb ecall checks.
